approach: Root cause: `refusing_check` (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks. None compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria, and no rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it. A reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7, 20261029-110953-bw7k; failed attempt 20261030-060839-1njk). The fix is `check_request_parts` as the last step, so every existing refusal keeps its check name. The design of the last round stands (shared `request_own_lines` filter; Enumerated and Bullet parts; distinctive-stem coverage; clause-scoped criterion negation; request-side deferral by marker citation; code-only enforcement). This round answers five findings. (F1) The person's corrections are request-side text: `refusing_check` gains one parameter, `corrections: &[String]`, right after `request`. `read_once` fills it from the `history` it already holds (the line that followed each earlier reading, via `athena correct` or an answer). The retried job's `attempt.corrections` are read inside `request_with_retried_parts`. The last step still reads `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));`, with `request` shadowed just before it by the retried request, the current request and one marked line per correction. A deferring correction accepts the reading. A correction that only mentions the part does not. (F2) The replay (`check_reading_text`, replay.rs:54-65) runs with no attempt and no corrections, so it sees neither. The measured share is stated as covering first-attempt requests only. Retries and corrections are covered by corpus proxy cases, and 'replay retries with their earlier attempt and corrections' is named as a follow-up. (F3) The error tells the reader the sure repair: cite the marker. (F4) The word lists are written once, as in code, and the 'test'/'tests'/'json' departure from criterion 3's wording is stated. (F5) Variant tests are table-driven, one case per demonstrated behaviour, with an explicit list of cases that can be dropped.

decisions.choice: 1. Build `request_parts` on a shared line filter. Factor the loop of `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189-208: ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR and APPROVAL_ANCHOR flags, stop at '## Source' for approved work, drop fenced lines, drop `is_generated_line` lines, terms.rs:62) into `pub(super) fn request_own_lines(request: &str) -> Vec<&str>`. `plain_request_prose` becomes `request_own_lines(request).into_iter().map(plain_line).join("\n")` with identical output. `request_parts` (topics.rs) reads only `request_own_lines`; for an approved-work request it skips the first line (the proposal title). RequestPart = {marker: Option<String>, kind: Enumerated|Bullet, text, group: Option<usize>, optional: bool}. `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` stay unchanged. terms.rs is a listed deliverable.
decisions.reason: Generated and copied text (approved-work '## Source' copies from work_decisions.rs, root-cause title and 'Cause:' lines from hestia.rs, fenced 'Request:' blocks) holds 'Acceptance:' bullets and numbered lists that must never become parts. One filter means a later change to the generated shapes is made once. `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs plan_entry; steward.rs:587) and the corpus pins its bullet counts, so it stays.

rejected.why: Misses fences and the approved-work '## Source' copy and drifts from terms.rs.

decisions.choice: 2. Placement, retries and corrections (finding 1). `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));` is the last `step!` in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references` (checks.rs:549); it returns Ok when `capability` is none or `question` is some, as `check_governance_coverage` does. The signature becomes `refusing_check(reading, request, corrections: &[String], attempt, referenced, repo_files)`. `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:492, signature unchanged, so run/tests.rs, replay.rs and the CLI are untouched) passes `&[]`. `read_once` (reading.rs:571; `history: &[(Reading, Option<String>)]` is in scope, the second element being the correction or answer that followed each earlier reading, built at reading.rs:1402-1414) passes `history.iter().filter_map(|(_, c)| c.clone())`. Directly before the step add `let request = &request_with_retried_parts(request, corrections, attempt);` (a new fn in topics.rs). It returns the retried job's `attempt.request`, a blank line, the current `request`, then one line per correction: first `attempt.corrections`, then the current `corrections`, each as `USER_CORRECTION_PREFIX` + the text with newlines turned into spaces. USER_CORRECTION_PREFIX = 'User correction (data, not a part): '. Only `attempt` is added; jobs in `referenced`, even followed-up ones, are not, and a retry of a retry is not chained. The shadow comes after every other step, so no other check sees it. Callers of `refusing_check` updated to pass `&[]` (or a case's corrections): reading.rs:720 (real value), tests at reading.rs:4820, 5142, 7284, 7289, 9096; refusal_corpus.rs:1094, 1116, 1159, 1189, 1207, 1213, 2771 (the `Case` struct at ~82 gets a `corrections: Vec<String>` field, default empty); checks.rs:499. The parser separates the prefixed lines first (`split_corrections(text) -> (body, Vec<&str>)`), so a correction like '1. add X' is never a part and never opens or ends an Acceptance section. Limits (doc comment, CHANGELOG, Risks): a retry that narrows scope in words outside the deferral list is refused until a criterion covers the part; a retried request that is itself a retry has no parts; a retried approved-work request stops at '## Source'.
decisions.reason: Finding 1 (critic, from reading.rs:1402-1424, 720-726 and retry.rs:808-810): `athena correct` stores a one-line correction and reads again; the reader follows 'leave (3) for a follow-up' and puts (3) in out_of_scope, and without this the check would tell the reader to cover it, against the user, who cannot edit the request after admission. The same holds for a retried job's carried corrections (`EarlierAttempt.corrections`, reader.rs:62). A retry's text is 'try again on <job>', so its parts come from `attempt.request` (reader.rs:40). Placing the step last keeps each existing Refuse case's check name; `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line and still works. A new parameter is one mechanical edit at each caller, all in deliverable files, and keeps `refusing_check` as the one function the source-order scans split on.

decisions.choice: 3. Parser kinds. `request_parts` runs over the body (corrections split off) of `request_own_lines` with states before / in section / after. Before the heading, Enumerated parts are line-start `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` and inline `(1)..(2)..` or `(a)..(b)..` sequences (start at 1 or a, consecutive, 2+ markers, each marker followed by text with a significant stem; the last part ends at the first '. ' or line end). The Acceptance section opens on a trimmed, case-insensitive line equal to `Acceptance:`, `Acceptance criteria:`, `## Acceptance` or `## Acceptance criteria`. Other headings are a stated limit. In the section, a line starting `-`, `*` or `N.` is a Bullet with marker None (no inline scan); `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` lines are Enumerated. Blank and indented lines stay in the section. The section ENDS at the first non-blank line with no leading whitespace that is not a list line. Marker-cited coverage and every marker-based deferral or negation apply only to Enumerated parts.
decisions.reason: Bullets have no marker, so criterion 2's own words 'leaves (3) out ... as a follow-up' do not number bullets by position. StewardRequest puts a `Files:` line after its bullets (steward.rs:581-585), and a later Notes list or copied block must not become required bullets. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and no heading; a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Only the exact line `Acceptance:` opens the section
rejected.why: Hand-written variants leave their bullets unenforced.

rejected.option: Number bullets by position so a marker can cite them
rejected.why: Criterion 2's '(3) ... follow-up' would cancel itself.

rejected.option: The section never ends, or Enumerated parsing resumes after it
rejected.why: A later Notes or Files list would become required parts.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part
rejected.why: False refusals over fixtures with free-form bullets.

decisions.choice: 4. Alternatives and optional parts, with real introducers only. An inline Enumerated sequence is one group when (i) the text before its first marker in the same sentence holds one of ALT_INTRODUCERS = 'one of the following', 'one of these', 'one of the options', 'one of:', 'pick one', 'choose one', 'choose between', 'pick between', 'either of'; or (ii) it holds 'either' and an ' or ' lies before the last marker; or (iii) the last marker is directly preceded by 'or' or ', or'. Contiguous line-start parts after a non-part line that holds an ALT_INTRODUCER are one group, and a part line ending ' or' groups with the next part. A bare 'pick', 'choose', 'one of' or 'either' with no 'or' groups nothing. A group is covered when any member is covered, skipped when every member is skipped, and the error names it. A part is optional, and skipped, when its text after the marker starts with 'optionally' or holds 'if time permits' or 'nice to have'. Groups apply to Enumerated parts only. Limits (doc comment): an 'or' inside one part's text is not a group; 'either' without markers is not read.
decisions.reason: 'Store it either as (a) a JSON file or (b) a TOML table.' must accept a reading that picks (a). Common lead-ins ('Pick up where job X left off: (1) .. (2) .. (3) ..', 'This is one of three fixes: (1) ..') must stay required parts. `out_of_scope` never covers, so without groups the only repair would be a criterion for work not being done.

rejected.option: Group on any 'pick', 'choose' or 'one of' before the first marker
rejected.why: Ordinary lead-ins would let a reading drop two of three parts silently.

rejected.option: Treat every (a)/(b) sequence as required parts
rejected.why: Refuses a reading that chose one option, with no honest repair.

rejected.option: Let any reading omit parts that contain 'or'
rejected.why: 'Add a flag or alias' style parts would never be enforced.

decisions.choice: 5. Stems (`part_stems`) with the word lists written once, as they will be in code (finding 4). FUNCTION_WORDS = the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now. COMMON_WORDS = the existing list at topics.rs:157-161 (it holds 'athena'). PART_FILLER = pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior. TEXT_PATH_WORDS (dropped from part text, criterion text and paths) = crates, src, core, lib, mod, bin, rs, md, toml, yml, yaml, lock, txt. PATH_ONLY_WORDS (dropped from deliverable paths only, in addition) = tests, test, json. Steps: strip a leading `[tag]`; criterion text only (`criterion_words`) is first cleaned: drop tokens holding '/', '_' or '::', drop backtick spans that start with `cargo` or `git`, and drop an unquoted span from the token `cargo` or `git` to the next of '.', ';', ',', ')' or the end (flags such as --json stay); then lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words, drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters; w stripped of one trailing 's' when longer than 3 is s; drop the word when w or s is in FUNCTION_WORDS, COMMON_WORDS, PART_FILLER or TEXT_PATH_WORDS; cut s to 6 chars; map `doc` to `docume`. `stems_match(a,b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other. Path stems of a deliverable path: split on non-alphanumerics, drop TEXT_PATH_WORDS and PATH_ONLY_WORDS, then the same FUNCTION/COMMON/FILLER drop and stemming. STATED DEPARTURE from criterion 3's wording: 'test'/'tests' and 'json' are ignored only in deliverable paths, not in part or criterion text, because 'a test fails when the timeout is missing' must still cover a test part and 'the --json flag' is a real stem. Worked examples in `part_stems_worked_examples`: 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; 'Add a core test for the timeout' = {test, timeou}; '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume, descri, json}? NO: the path token docs/guide.md is dropped, so the set is {descri, json}; the path adds {docume, guide} only when it is a deliverable the criterion contains (and the alias keeps '(2) Document the flag in the guide' covered by it); 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}; criterion '[behavior] Run cargo test -p athena-core --test timeout' = {}; path stems of crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs = {foo}. `request_parts_path_words_are_ignored` pins all four lists (TEXT_PATH_WORDS, PATH_ONLY_WORDS, FUNCTION_WORDS, PART_FILLER) by name and content and the departure.
decisions.reason: A stock `cargo test -p athena-core` criterion had stems {core, test} and covered a dropped 'core test' part; now it has none. The pooled path stems (decision 6) are the only path contribution. The alias keeps 'docs/guide.md describes --json' covering '(2) Document the flag in the guide' because the deliverable docs/guide.md contributes {docume, guide}.

rejected.option: Apply path words only to deliverable paths
rejected.why: Criterion text keeps core and test from commands and paths.

rejected.option: Drop `test` from all stems
rejected.why: 'a test fails when the timeout is missing' must still cover a test part.

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: 6. Coverage and error text. For each kind with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind (fallback to the full set if that empties a part); n is the remaining count; need = min(2,n) for Enumerated, min(1,n) for Bullet; n = 0 is skipped. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the path stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least `need` stems with it, or (c) a usable criterion cites the marker of an Enumerated part (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. A deliverable path alone never covers. `out_of_scope` never covers. The error names each uncovered part (marker plus text) or group, the cause, each ignored criterion with its phrase, and says: 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion' and, for an Enumerated part (finding 3), 'or cite its marker, for example "part (3)", in a criterion that names its subject'; and 'unless the request itself defers it'. `request_parts_error_names_the_part_and_the_repair` asserts all of these strings.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3: a path alone does not cover a part. Dropping shared stems stops a criterion for part (2) covering part (3) through the shared subject 'flag'. Finding 3: the marker citation is the repair that always works (rule (c) needs one distinctive stem), and this job's own criteria use it ('part 2'). The reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759), so the error must name the sure repair. The tension (stricter refuses more reworded readings, looser misses dropped parts) is named in the doc comment.

rejected.option: Keep rule (b), a deliverable path alone covers, with generic path words removed
rejected.why: Still lets a path cover a part with no criterion.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to its one best part
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules than dropping shared stems.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: The summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: 7. Criterion-side negation is scoped to a clause and to the part. DEFER_PHRASES: follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. CRITERION_NEGATION = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of. CRITERION_MARKER_NEGATION = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. `negation_hit(criterion, part)` splits the criterion into clauses at '. ', '; ', ', ', ': ' and ' and ', ' but ', ' while ', ' so '. A clause is relevant when it holds a word whose stem matches a distinctive stem of the part, or (marker list, Enumerated parts only) cites the part's marker. A CRITERION_NEGATION phrase in a relevant clause, or a marker-list phrase in a marker-citing clause, makes the criterion unusable for that part, unless the part's own text holds the phrase. A criterion unusable for one part may cover another. The error lists each ignored criterion with its phrase. Bullets have no marker, so only CRITERION_NEGATION in a relevant clause applies.
decisions.reason: Criteria here often describe refusal behaviour ('moves it to out_of_scope as a follow-up'); the phrase cancels only next to the part's own subject. 'The timeout test is deferred' still cannot cover part (3); 'status lists skipped checks' still covers '(2) Report skipped checks in status'.

rejected.option: Count a phrase anywhere in the criterion
rejected.why: Cancels criteria that mention refusal in another clause.

rejected.option: A flat list where skipped, omitted and excluded cancel every criterion
rejected.why: Refuses 'status lists skipped checks'.

decisions.choice: 8. Request-side deferral, including corrections. A part is skipped as deferred when (i) its own text holds a DEFER_PHRASES phrase ('(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job'), or (ii) another sentence of the body of `request_own_lines`, taken outside every part span (spans blanked before splitting at '. ', '! ', '? ' and newlines), cites its marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c` or `item c` and holds a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase in some clause, or (iii) a correction line (split-off prefixed lines of decision 2: the current job's corrections, the retried job's corrections) has a sentence with a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase in a clause that cites the part's marker, or whose clause shares at least `need` distinctive stems with the part (this stem route is for corrections only, because a correction is the person speaking about this job and often names the subject, not the number). REQUEST_DEFERRAL is criterion 4's words with close variants only: 'out of scope', 'out-of-scope', 'for now', 'defer', 'deferred', 'follow-up', 'follow up', 'followup', and 'later' in the restricted forms 'later' as the last word of its clause, 'at a later', 'for later', 'for a later', 'come later'. Skip, skipped, omitted and excluded are NOT request-side words. Clauses are split at '; ', ', ', ': ', ' but ', ' while '. The negator guard (not, n't, never, cannot, after removing 'not in this job', 'not part of', 'not done', 'not covered') applies only to the clause that holds the deferral phrase. So 'Part (3) is out of scope for now; do not touch athena.toml.' defers (3), 'Part (3) must not be deferred.' does not, 'In (2), skip blank lines.' and 'For (1), excluded files are listed.' do not, 'In (2), later entries override earlier ones.' does not (bare 'later' mid-clause). The same scan runs over the retried request and the retry text. Correction cases: 'leave (3) for a follow-up, it is done elsewhere' defers (3); 'leave the timeout test for a follow-up' defers a part sharing {timeou, test}; 'make sure (3) is covered' does not defer. '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately', '(3) Defer the flush until exit', '(3) Add a latest-value column' stay required. Stated departure from criterion 4: bare 'later' inside a part's own text ('(3) Add the dashboard later') does not defer it. 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' cites only part 2; a stated limit.
decisions.reason: Marker citation guards against stray words; the clause-scoped negator guard keeps a clarifying second clause from flipping the result; matching criterion 4's words keeps 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.' working. Finding 1: the user's corrections are the one way a person defers a part after admission, so the check must not contradict them.

rejected.option: Whole-sentence negator guard
rejected.why: A later 'do not touch athena.toml' clause would leave an explicitly deferred part required.

rejected.option: Broad list (skip, skipped, omitted, excluded) on the request side
rejected.why: 'In (2), skip blank lines.' would defer a part the request wants done.

rejected.option: Narrow DEFER_PHRASES only for request sentences
rejected.why: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' would leave the part required.

rejected.option: Ignore corrections for the deferral scan
rejected.why: The check would tell the reader to cover a part the user just deferred (finding 1).

decisions.choice: 9. Enforce by code only. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say why information alone is not enough: the reader already sees the request and still deferred part (3) in jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, so a refusal rule is the allowed fix. 'Pass the parsed request parts to the reader' is named as a follow-up, not done. No prompt is edited (reader budget 1998 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md). The refusal text reaches the reader on its one corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759).
decisions.reason: No token headroom in the reader prompt, and a prompt line is not a mechanism.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: No budget; prose only.

rejected.option: Build the parsed parts into the reader brief now
rejected.why: A larger change across briefs and budgets.

decisions.choice: 10. Measure with the producer-loop replay, and state what it cannot see (finding 2). The producer loop runs `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294-2319) once the change touches `crates/` (`touches_reading_rules`, replay.rs:314); the limit is `replay_limit_percent(declared)` = declared 10 + 5 (replay.rs:304-308). `replay_cases` (replay.rs:142-157) carries only `request.text` and the reading, and `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54-65) passes `attempt = None`, no referenced jobs and (after this change) `&[]` corrections, whose doc comment says there are no earlier attempts. So the replay checks recorded first-attempt requests only: a recorded retry replays as the bare text 'try again on <job>' (no parts, always accepted, which also pads the denominator), and a reading accepted after a correction that deferred a part replays without that correction. The producer classifies each newly refused reading as (real drop) or (false refusal: reworded part, deferral wording, list shape) and fixes only false refusals in the matcher, adding a corpus case for each shape. A newly refused reading whose accepted reading followed a recorded correction is an artifact of the replay, not a matcher gap: the report counts it separately and does not loosen the matcher for it. The report states the measured share and says it stands for first-attempt requests only; it never states or implies a retry or correction share. Retries and corrections are covered by corpus proxy cases (decision 11) and the follow-up 'replay retries with their earlier attempt and corrections' (needs `check-reading` to take them) is named in the doc comment and CHANGELOG. The declared 10% and the margin are never raised, no stored reading is edited. With no records the report says 'no replay: <reason>' and that 10% is an estimate.
decisions.reason: The 10% is an unmeasured estimate (records/ is absent from the snapshot), and a share above the limit fails the job late at the verification hold. Counting retries as accepts would make the measured share look lower than the real refusal rate.

rejected.option: Count 'a retried request' as a replay-classified refusal kind
rejected.why: The replay never runs the retry path (finding 2).

rejected.option: Rely on the hold at verification alone
rejected.why: The producer would never see the list.

rejected.option: Raise the declared share to fit the measured result
rejected.why: It hides a matcher gap.

rejected.option: Make the replay carry attempts and corrections now
rejected.why: It changes `check-reading`, `replay_cases` and the records read, outside the deliverables; named as a follow-up.

decisions.choice: 11. Size and test shape (finding 5). Unit tests are table-driven: one test `request_parts_refused_when_part_three_is_left_out` loops over variants a-m as (name, reading edit, expected refusal) rows; one `request_parts_retry_and_corrections` over the retry and correction rows; one `request_parts_request_defers` over the deferral sentences; one `request_parts_alternatives_and_optional` over introducers and lead-ins; one `request_parts_heading_variants_and_section_end` over the four headings and the section end; plus `part_stems_worked_examples`, `request_parts_path_words_are_ignored`, `request_parts_error_names_the_part_and_the_repair`, `request_parts_skip_copied_and_generated_text`, `plain_request_prose_is_unchanged_by_the_shared_filter`, `request_parts_doc_names_root_cause_and_step`. Corpus: one case per demonstrated behaviour (ids in the demonstrations). If the run runs short, these cases may be dropped without dropping any criterion's demonstration: `request-parts-excluded-word-does-not-defer`, `request-parts-later-entries-does-not-defer`, `request-parts-future-word-part-dropped`, `request-parts-separately-and-defer-words-stay-required`, `request-parts-choose-sensible-names-is-not-a-group`, `request-parts-one-of-three-fixes-is-not-a-group`, `request-parts-if-time-permits-part`, `request-parts-nice-to-have-part`, `request-parts-star-bullet-dropped`, `request-parts-heading-acceptance-criteria-colon`, `request-parts-bullet-criterion-mentions-marker-of-no-bullet`. Their rows stay in the table-driven unit tests, which are cheap. The two steps that must not be cut are the retry/correction rows and the sza7/bw7k cases.
decisions.reason: Table rows cost a line each; separate tests and cases cost a function each. The earlier attempt failed in planning; a plan a producer can finish in one run is part of the fix.

rejected.option: One test and one corpus case per variant
rejected.why: Over 60 cases and 20 tests, too much for one run.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion; stricter matching refuses more, looser misses dropped parts. Cleaning criterion text removes stems a criterion used to contribute.
risks.mitigation: Tension named in the doc comment. Bullets need one distinctive stem; n = 0 parts are skipped; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers an Enumerated part; one criterion pools with the paths it names; the error names the part, both repairs (a criterion, or a cited marker) and each ignored criterion, and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy tests guard the common case. The 10% is an estimate; the loop replay (step 12) measures first-attempt requests.

risks.risk: Retries and corrections are not measured by the replay (replay.rs:54-65 runs with no attempt, no corrections), and the retry path is the riskiest: a retried request may hold parts the earlier job already landed or the user agreed to narrow, so a retry is refused on parts the person no longer wants.
risks.mitigation: State this in the doc comment, CHANGELOG and the report; never report a share for retries. Only the retried job's request is added. The retry text's sentences and all corrections count for deferral. The error names the part and two repairs. Corpus proxy cases pin retry covered, retry deferred by text, deferred by correction, dropped, and the landed-part limit (needs a regression criterion). Follow-up named: replay retries with their earlier attempt and corrections.

risks.risk: A correction is read as a deferral when it is not (stem route matches a clause naming the part's subject next to 'later'), or a deferring correction worded without the REQUEST_DEFERRAL words is missed and the reader is told to cover the part.
risks.mitigation: Corrections need a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase, a per-clause negator guard and a marker citation or `need` distinctive stems. A missed one is refused with text that names the repair, and the user can correct again. Corpus: deferring, only-mentions and retry-carried rows.

risks.mitigation: All callers are in deliverable files (listed in dependents). The function keeps its name and body shape, so the scans that split on `pub fn refusing_check(` still work; `cargo test --locked` compiles and runs all of them. risks.risk: A request sentence that cites a marker with a deferral word is read as a deferral when it is not ('In (2), later entries ...', 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' naming only part 2).
risks.mitigation: Marker citation is required; 'later' counts only in restricted forms; the negator guard is per clause; skip, skipped, omitted and excluded are not request-side words. Corpus and table rows pin it; 'Parts N and M' lists are a stated limit.

risks.risk: Bare 'later' in a part's own text is not a deferral, so a reading that follows '(3) Add the dashboard later' is refused (stated departure from criterion 4).
risks.mitigation: Stated in the doc comment and pinned by `request-parts-part-own-text-later-stays-required`; the request or a correction can defer with a sentence naming the marker.

risks.risk: Alternatives grouping misses a form or reads an introducer where none was meant.
risks.mitigation: Groups need a phrase that introduces alternatives or an ' or ' before the last marker; bare 'pick', 'choose' and 'one of' group nothing; limits are in the doc comment; table rows and corpus cases cover each form and the lead-ins.

The call is `refusing_check(reading, request, corrections, attempt, &[], None)` (through the updated `refuser_for` at reading.rs:7288). Rows: (a) part 3 absent: Some("check_request_parts"); (b) part 3 only in `out_of_scope` as a follow-up: same; (c) criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing' added: None and `check_reading_acceptance` Ok; (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused; (e) criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted; (f) 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' in the reading's criteria: still refused; (g) 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later': refused; (h) 'The timeout test is deferred': refused; (i) '(2) Report skipped checks in status' with 'status lists skipped checks': covered; (j) 'Part (2) skipped checks are omitted': ignored, error names it and 'omitted'; (k) criterion 'a reading that moves the flag to a follow-up job is refused, and the timeout test passes' added to (a): accepted; (l) 'the timeout test is moved to a follow-up job': refused; (m) deliverable tests/timeout.rs added, no criterion: refused; (n) retry: attempt = `EarlierAttempt` (helper `earlier(job)` at reading.rs:4382) whose `request` holds parts (1)-(3), current request 'try again on <job>', reading drops (3): refused; with (3) covered: accepted; (o) the request has Acceptance bullets and one has no criterion: refused (Bullet case). The error asserts hold the strings 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion' and 'cite its marker, for example "part (3)"' for an Enumerated part. `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts the stem sets of decision 5.
